title: The AI Slop Dominos Begin to Fall
author: ExoHerb
selftext:
Slotbound. 

Is there anything else to say?

I listened to about 15 minutes of some random YouTube video talking about AI games. They said something that I have been commenting on for a little while.

As long as your game is good, no one actually cares how it was made. End of story.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I agree about code. And I don’t know why but I do think some of the anti ai people are kind of right about art sometimes. We’ve all seen it, when ai is used carelessly for art it can be really off putting for some reason. Fortunately for slotbound the art is minimal enough for it to not have that effect so bad, but the art is super generic… which may not matter for some games as much lol.

comments.author: PHNTMS_exe
comments.body: I mean, yeah.

comments.author: ByteHavenGames
comments.body:
Before AI slop there were asset flips. We had nearly 10k+ releases per year in 2021 before mass produced AI slop when everyone and their mother were making video games because there was nothing else to do in the middle of pandemic. Does it really matter if the number is 10k or 30k? 

Either number is completely out of any single player's capabilities to effectively parse through. That's why storefronts are algorithmic these days. Most of the slop never gets 10+ reviews necessary to gain any visibility on Steam and is pushed down and not seen by anyone. The same as it worked with asset flips 5-6 years ago.

comments.author: ByteHavenGames
comments.body:
Your argument can be somewhat true and also ineffective in predicting general market success, most gamers are not artists. It also hedges on a lot of what ifs and maybes.

Historically, most players haven't given a shit about code a single bit so it's not a generalization, it's just a statement of fact that is objectively true. I don't see large swaths of population suddenly starting to care about something they never actually directly see or have the ability to critique.   
  
People can't change perception about things that are imperceptible to them and most people are not idealogically driven to decry everything AI outside reddit and bluesky.

replies.author: Good-Acanthaceae-136
replies.body:
It doesn't have to be artists. Any person that loses money or work in the future due to AI is probably not going to be an avid supporter of anything that uses AI.

So far AI has mostly only hit creative industries and still not that much damage has been done yet, once more people start being affected negatively in other industries views and opinions are going to change.

It's just the way most people are, people don't care about anything until they are the ones being affected. That's why predominately the people against AI right now are creatives.

comments.author: ByteHavenGames
comments.body:
Go back to 2021 and you have thousands of asset flips per every successful game. It has always been a thing since game engines like Unity and Unreal became publicly available and Steam opened the floodgates. Sure, the scale is different now, but I don't think it matters much in algorithmically driven marketplaces that push most of the slop down into irrelevance.   
  
You didn't see the asset flips on Steam 5-6 years ago same as you don't see the AI slop now. Everyone's just doomposting about total numberts without context of real world impact.

comments.author: RemarkableWish2508
comments.body:
Wasn't there a game that would take an eternity to load savegames... until someone realized that it was running a JSON parser in a loop on a massive bunch of useless trash, and fixed it with an unofficial patch?

---

That game is Grand Theft Auto Online

In February 2021, a programmer known as t0st reverse-engineered the game's PC version to figure out why loading into an online session took up to six minutes or more. They discovered two major bottlenecks in the game's code when loading the 10 MB catalog of in-game store items:

* Inefficient JSON parsing. The game used sscanf to read a massive 10 MB JSON file containing around 63,000 items. Internally, this caused the program to repeatedly count the length of the entire remaining string (strlen) for every single value parsed.
* Slow duplicate checks. After parsing each item, the code checked its hash against every single previously loaded item to prevent duplicates. This resulted in nearly two billion unnecessary checks on startup.

The Fix and Aftermath

* Community patch. t0st created a proof-of-concept patch that cached the string length and bypassed the redundant duplicate checks, cutting loading times by roughly 70% (dropping a six-minute load down to under two minutes).
* Official update. Rockstar Games confirmed the findings, integrated the fix into an official update a few weeks later, and awarded t0st a $10,000 bug bounty.

I regularly stop every few days to do a code audit with Astra just to tighten the code and squeeze more FPS. This kind of audit is now trivial.

comments.author: PonSquaredJapan
comments.body:
I really wish this was true.  The second I put anything AI or Vibe Coded next to my game I am downvoted to infinity.  No one even gives me feedback past "SLOP" and no downloads.  Its super frustrating.  Pouring my heart and soul into something, spending hundreds of hours working on it, learning so many new things, and its hand waved off before its even played.

I really hope things change soon.

comments.author: Interesting-Rent5630
comments.body: Speaking of dominoes, I used Codex and Claude to create TEXAS DOMINOES.  It seems to resonate well with the older crowd, and they certainly don't care that AI was involved.  As long as the game is easy to play and fun for them, that is all they are concerned with.

comments.author: Silent_Principle_392
comments.body:
Ai code is already pretty much accepted by the mainstream. 

AI art will be a much bigger hurdle for most even if it’s really good ai generated assets it’s just inherently something that people enjoy the effort as much as the outcome. 

Same with music, artists are looked up too more when they can sing, write, and play instruments. Even if the song would sound the exact same if someone else wrote the lyrics and a band did all the instruments.

So a game dev that writes their own code, does their own assets and music will likely be more popular and respected in the scene. Even when AI will be able to do all of it better than them.

At least that’s my theory 🤷
